Purpose: open the selected packed level file and backward-expand its title and playable occupants. Inputs: three-byte filename at `$117D` (`nn*`), device 8, packed stream from the current disk side. Outputs: title occupant first, then after fire the playable occupant; returns at end of file. Assumptions: KERNAL serial input is available whenever `$01=$37`; header cursors bound valid output. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, `$02`, `$F6-$FF`, coding-table tail `$17F3-$17F5`, file/channel state. Hardware changes: replaces IRQ vector low byte temporarily, switches `$01` among all-RAM and KERNAL/I/O-visible states, polls CIA 1 fire, silences SID, and uses VIC border writes as read activity indication. Actual bytes are written from `upper` down through `lower+1`.
function: undefined LoadAndExpandLevelFile()

Purpose: Store the first already-read byte of a packed level header, read the remainder of the eight-byte loader header, and continue the resident backward decompression path.
Inputs: A is the first header byte and X=0. The KERNAL-backed byte reader at $EE13 is available; the current level file/channel is open; loader pass counter $02 and packed-stream state are valid.
Outputs: Stores A in $FB, reads four further bytes into $FC-$FF (upper output cursor $FC/$FD and lower bound $FE/$FF), then reads exactly three more bytes through STA $17EE,X for X=5,6,7, filling the header-supplied distance-width slots $17F3-$17F5. The complete header is eight bytes. It then clears $F6-$FA and expands the selected occupant. On the pass boundary it re-enters this same header tail at $1029 for the next segment.
Assumptions: The packed file supplies one seed byte, four cursor/bound bytes and three distance-width bytes - eight header bytes in total - and every decoded destination remains within the header's lower/upper bounds.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $01 transiently, $02, $F6-$FF, $17F3-$17F5, destination memory, loader stack frames, and KERNAL file/channel state along the continued load path.
Hardware changes: The continued loader switches CPU-port $01 between all-RAM and KERNAL/I/O-visible mappings, uses KERNAL serial input, polls CIA 1 at $DC00/$DC01 on the pass boundary, silences SID at $D418, and writes VIC-II border $D020 during byte reads.

Purpose: Return the next packed-stream bit, refill the sentinel-marked one-byte reservoir when it empties, and perform the exact inter-segment or final-load transition when the output cursor reaches its boundary. Inputs: Bit reservoir $FB; destination cursor $FC/$FD; segment boundary $FE/$FF; remaining-segment state $02; KERNAL serial-input status $90; and an active packed input channel. Outputs: On an ordinary path carry is the next decoded bit and $FB holds the shifted or renewed reservoir. Boundary paths close or advance the input, return to the loaded phase, or display the preceding title and wait before decoding the next segment. Assumptions: Callers consume carry immediately; $EE13 is callable only with KERNAL ROM visible at $01=$37; the decompressor otherwise uses its all-RAM mapping; and the saved A value and return stack have the layout established by the decoder. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, stack, $01, $02, $90, $FB, and transition scratch on boundary paths. Hardware changes: Temporarily changes CPU-port banking; boundary paths may clear and close the KERNAL channel, enable interrupts, poll CIA 1, tick music, silence SID volume, and invoke the phase title renderer.

Purpose: Select literal-input mode by writing SEC at the shared copy-mode instruction, then fall through to the backward token-copy loop so every output byte comes from KERNAL serial input. Inputs: Run/page state $F7/$F8; destination cursor $FC/$FD; page companion $FA; an active KERNAL input channel; and writable code at $1151. Outputs: Literal bytes are read through $EE13 and stored backward through ($FC),Y; $F8/$FA and $FC/$FD advance to the next decode position while $F7 is preserved. Assumptions: $1151 is writable RAM, $1142 is the shared token-copy tail, and KERNAL input is available while $01=$37. Clobbers: A, Y, flags, $F8, $FA, $FC/$FD, $01, self-modified byte $1151, and border color $D020; X, $F7, and $F9 are preserved. Hardware changes: Each serial read exposes KERNAL ROM, restores the decoder's $01=$30 RAM mapping, and increments then normalizes VIC-II border color $D020 as a load indicator.

Purpose: Execute the shared backward token-copy loop, taking bytes from the LZ match pointer in CLC mode or from KERNAL serial input in SEC mode. Inputs: Run/page state $F7/$F8; match pointer $F9/$FA; destination cursor $FC/$FD; and mode opcode CLC $18 or SEC $38 self-installed at $1151. Outputs: Decoded bytes are stored backward through ($FC),Y; $F8/$FA and $FC/$FD advance to the next token position while $F7 and $F9 are preserved. Assumptions: The decoder installed the correct mode at $1151 and all match, destination, and segment bounds describe the active backward-expanded segment. Clobbers: A, Y, flags, $F8, $FA, and $FC/$FD; literal mode also changes $01 and $D020. X and $F7/$F9 are preserved. Hardware changes: Match mode has no I/O effect. Literal mode exposes KERNAL ROM, reads through $EE13, restores $01=$30, and updates VIC-II border color $D020.

Purpose: add a packed two-nibble amount into the status-digit array beginning at digit 3, propagate decimal carries left, and request a score redraw. Inputs: A holds two decimal nibbles; `$1CA0-$1CA5` holds display-encoded digits. Outputs: updated digits and `$0292=$FF`. Assumptions: every nibble is 0–9 and each stored digit uses the renderer's `$1B-$24` encoding. Clobbers: A, X, flags, and one temporary stack byte. Hardware changes: none.

Purpose: add a packed two-nibble amount into the status-digit array beginning at digit 4, propagate decimal carries left, and request a score redraw. Inputs: A holds two decimal nibbles; `$1CA0-$1CA5` holds display-encoded digits. Outputs: updated digits and `$0292=$FF`. Assumptions: every nibble is 0–9 and each stored digit uses the renderer's `$1B-$24` encoding. Clobbers: A, X, flags, and one temporary stack byte. Hardware changes: none.

Purpose: Add the two decimal nybbles in A to the score-display digit selected by X and propagate decimal carry toward more significant digits.
Inputs: A contains two packed decimal digits; X is 3 for the hundreds-entry caller or 4 for the tens-entry caller; score-display digit codes occupy $1CA0,X and lower indices, with $25 as the first code past digit 9.
Outputs: Adds A's low nybble to digit X modulo ten, adds the high nybble plus carry to digit X-1, propagates further carry toward lower indices, stores the updated display codes, sets score-dirty latch $0292=$FF, returns A=$FF, and preserves Y.
Assumptions: Each source nybble is 0-9 and every score cell initially contains a valid digit code below $25; binary arithmetic is active.
Clobbers: A, X, N, V, Z, C, affected score bytes in the $1CA0 row, and $0292; Y, D, and I are preserved. The balanced PHA/PHP/PLA/PLP sequence restores its temporary stack state before RTS.
Hardware changes: No hardware registers are accessed; $1CA0 is the resident score display buffer in RAM.

Purpose: clear logical sprite slots 4–7 and their prepared Y coordinates, then clear animation/script state `$63`. Inputs: none. Outputs: `$0214-$0217`, `$024C-$024F`, and `$63` are zero. Assumptions: low workspace is writable. Clobbers: A, X, flags. Hardware changes: none; only RAM staging state changes.

Purpose: synchronize three engine time baselines with the current 50 Hz tick. Inputs: tick byte `$E2`. Outputs: `$026C`, `$026E`, and `$0277` receive the same tick value. Assumptions: the gameplay IRQ maintains `$E2`. Clobbers: A and flags. Hardware changes: none.
Three zero bytes after ResetEngineTickBaselines, up to the page boundary where reverse_multicolor_pairs starts at $1200; nothing in this load reads them.

Complete 256-entry byte lookup reversing two-bit pairs. Every table entry has been checked against the reversal formula. The renderer and sprite blitter use the original source byte as X; $1200 reverses four multicolor pixel pairs, while $1300 reverses eight high-resolution bits. This table covers $1200-$12FF.

Complete 256-entry byte lookup reversing individual bits. Every table entry has been checked against the reversal formula. The renderer and sprite blitter use the original source byte as X; $1200 reverses four multicolor pixel pairs, while $1300 reverses eight high-resolution bits. This table covers $1300-$13FF.

Purpose: cold entry for a level-load cycle. Inputs: resident state and selected level number. Outputs: transfers permanently to the load coordinator after hardware initialization. Assumptions: resident code and `$3FF6` initialization vector are installed. Clobbers: X, stack pointer, decimal flag, interrupt state. Hardware changes: disables IRQ, clears decimal mode, resets SP to `$12`, calls the phase initialization vector, then jumps to `$16AF`; does not return.
function: undefined StartLevelLoad()

Purpose: tail-call the resident raster-synchronized bitmap-display setup at `$150A` through its stable veneer. Inputs: none; VIC-II I/O must be visible and its raster counter must advance. Outputs: returns after raster low byte reaches zero with raster high bit clear, border black, multicolor bitmap mode selected, 40-column timing selected, and `$D018=$18`. Assumptions: `$150A` and the active VIC bank's bitmap/screen data are installed. Clobbers: A and processor flags; X and Y are preserved. Hardware changes: the target polls `$D012` and `$D011` bit 7, then writes `$D020=$00`, `$D011=$3B`, `$D016=$18`, and `$D018=$18`; the veneer adds no stack frame.
function: undefined ScreenSetupVeneer()

Purpose: tail-call the resident display-workspace clearing routine at `$1478` through its stable veneer. Inputs: none; the resident bitmap, screen, and control workspaces must be writable. Outputs: clears `$0210/$0218/$0248`, bitmap spans in `$2000-$35FF`, and `$02A9`, and fills screen rows `$0800-$0AC5` with code `$10`. Assumptions: `$1478` is intact and the listed ranges are RAM. Clobbers: A, Y, and processor flags; X is preserved. Hardware changes: none; all target writes are RAM workspace updates and the veneer adds no stack frame.
function: undefined ScreenRendererVeneer()

Purpose: tail-call the resident tile/color compositor at `$17F6` through its stable veneer. Inputs: `$04/$05` points to an eight-byte tile; `$0E/$0F` to destination bitmap rows; `$10/$11` and `$12/$13` to packed screen-color descriptions; `$14/$15` to the paired color descriptor; `$E8` selects source order. Outputs: reconciled packed colors are written through `($10),Y`, `($12),Y`, and `($14),Y`, and eight transformed rows are merged through `($0E),Y`. Assumptions: all pointers and the `$1200` lookup are valid; a `$D800` destination requires I/O-visible color RAM. Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, compositor scratch `$0A-$41`, `$BC-$BE`, `$E3-$E9`, and `$0112-$011A`. Hardware changes: no register writes; the target writes color RAM only when `$14/$15` selects `$D800`; the veneer adds no stack frame.
function: undefined ResidentKernelVeneer()

Inputs: none; VIC-II raster registers must be visible

Purpose: install and start the gameplay interrupt system. Inputs: CIA Timer A latch bytes `$028C/$028D`. Outputs: raster line zero armed, CIA 1 Timer A running continuously, underlying IRQ vector `$FFFE/$FFFF=$1E15`, KERNAL CINV `$0314/$0315=$1E06`, and `$0231=0`. Assumptions: I/O is visible while the underlying RAM vectors are writable under the selected banking state. Clobbers: A and flags; returns with interrupts enabled. Hardware changes: programs VIC-II `$D011/$D012/$D019/$D01A`, CIA 1 `$DC04/$DC05/$DC0D/$DC0E`, both IRQ vectors, and the processor interrupt mask.
$40, an rti, and the whole NMI handler: the NMI vectors at $0318 and $FFFA both point here, so pressing RESTORE does nothing.

Purpose: render a variable-length text record embedded immediately after the caller JSR. Inputs: return address on stack followed by column, row, bitmap/color attributes, then nonzero character codes terminated by zero. Outputs: glyph bytes copied into bitmap memory, screen/color attributes written, and a synthesized return address pointing after the terminator. Assumptions: record and glyph tables are valid and writable bitmap/screen/color RAM is mapped. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, `$02-$09`, `$34/$35`, `$4A/$4B`. Hardware changes: color writes address the `$D800` color-RAM window when I/O is visible; other output targets bitmap and screen RAM.
function: undefined RenderInlineTextRecord()

Indexed base alias used by LDA $159D,Y at $BDFF with Y=$F8-$FF: its effective reads are the clipping masks at $1695-$169C. This address is also the operand byte of STA $34 at $159C, inside the inline-text renderer; it is not a routine boundary. The following renderer advances the inline text pointer and handles record end/continuation controls.

Inline-text pointer advance continuation: carry increments pointer high byte $05. The next character byte supplies four control bits; $15B6 advances $04/$05, then character bits select glyph data and plotting position. This is inside $1583, not a separate called routine.

25 little-endian screen-row addresses: $0400 + 40*row for rows 0-24. $15E0 doubles the text row index; $15E2/$15EA add the text column to this base before writing screen attributes. This table ends at $1662.

High-byte indexed alias of the little-endian pointer/row directory starting at $1631. The consumer doubles its logical index before the paired reads; no separate high-byte allocation begins here. The owning directory describes its full extent.

25 little-endian bitmap-row addresses: $2000 + 320*row for rows 0-24. $160D shifts the text column by three and adds these row bases before copying eight glyph bitmap rows. This table ends at $1694, immediately before the clipping masks.

High-byte indexed alias of the little-endian pointer/row directory starting at $1663. The consumer doubles its logical index before the paired reads; no separate high-byte allocation begins here. The owning directory describes its full extent.
Eight clipping masks $FF,$FE,$FC,$F8,$F0,$E0,$C0,$80. The blitter reads them directly with a nonnegative index at $BDE4, or through base $159D with wrapped negative offsets $F8-$FF at $BDFF.

Eight low address bytes 0,$40,$80,$C0 repeated twice, paired with $16A5 high bytes $0C/$0D. $98AA/$98B5 choose the actor slot and display-buffer phase, then add three-byte-per-row vertical offset when masking sprite pixels. The pointed staging buffers start at $0C00-$0DC0.
Eight high-byte values paired with the eight low bytes at $169D. The condition renderer adds its selected display-page bit before using $06/$07 as the target sprite-row pointer.

Purpose: coordinate a numbered level load while preserving the low C64 workspace needed by the caller. Inputs: level selector in `$EC`; filename digit destination `$117E`. Outputs: loaded phase, restored `$0000-$03FF`, marker `$0267=$FF`, then transfer through `$3FF3`. Assumptions: KERNAL initialization calls are visible under `$01=$37`; `$0C00-$0FFF` is temporary save space. Clobbers: A, X, flags and loader scratch; does not return after final handoff. Hardware changes: saves/restores zero page, stack, screen/vectors; resets KERNAL/CIA/VIC state and calls the loader before jumping to the selected phase entry.
function: undefined CoordinateLevelLoad()

Purpose: request disk side two when A is character `3`, wait for the shared Space/control-port-1-fire line to be released, render `INSERT SIDE TWO` and `PRESS SPACE`, then wait for that line to be pressed. Inputs: A contains the side/level character. Outputs: prompt rendered and input acknowledged for side two, otherwise immediate return. Assumptions: resident inline renderer and screen veneer are active. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, renderer scratch, and the stacked return address through `$1583`. Hardware changes: writes `$DC00=$7F` to select keyboard column 7 and reads CIA 1 port B `$DC01` bit 4, which is Space's matrix line and is shared with control-port-1 fire.
function: undefined HandleDiskSidePrompt()

Inline text after JSR $1583 at $1732: X=7, Y=6, colour fields $07/$B0, then 15 glyph codes and a zero terminator at $1748. The renderer masks each code to six bits and copies eight bytes from $1AE8 + 8*glyph. Decoded glyph sequence: 'INSERT SIDE TWO'. It resumes execution at $1749.

Inline text after JSR $1583 at $1749: X=9, Y=8, colour fields $07/$B0, then 11 glyph codes and a zero terminator at $175B. The renderer masks each code to six bits and copies eight bytes from $1AE8 + 8*glyph. Decoded glyph sequence: 'PRESS SPACE'. It resumes execution at $175C.

Selects keyboard column with CIA1 $DC00=$7F, polls the AND of $DC01 and $DC00 until shared bit 4 is low, calls the screen-renderer veneer and returns at $176E. Accepts the Space key or a corresponding joystick-fire line; it does not wait for all keys to be released.

Purpose: wait until the shared Space/control-port-1-fire line is released before displaying and accepting the disk-side prompt. Inputs: CIA 1 keyboard/control-port lines. Outputs: returns through the screen-renderer veneer when bit 4 is high. Assumptions: Space and control-port-1 fire are active low on the selected shared line. Clobbers: A and flags. Hardware changes: writes `$DC00=$7F` to select keyboard column 7, then polls CIA 1 port B `$DC01` bit 4 and jumps to `$140E` after release.

Eight retained compression-header/coding bytes $17E6-$17ED, initialized/used by the resident loader at $108A. Separate five-byte group begins at $17EE; the following three bytes $17F3-$17F5 complete the preserved coding header before executable compositor $17F6. Five loader parameters $17EE-$17F2, directly read by $1033 during decompression setup. They adjoin the eight-byte group at $17E6 and the three-byte coding tail; interpretation requires the resident loader phase, not the graphics decoder.
Three retained compression-header values 1,2,2 at $17F3-$17F5 immediately before the compositor entry $17F6. This is the known header tail; a full encoding contract is still open.

Purpose: decode one source tile, reconcile its two encoded color descriptions, and merge its eight rows into the destination multicolor bitmap
Inputs: $04/$05 points to the eight-byte source tile; $0E/$0F points to destination bitmap rows; $10/$11 and $12/$13 point to packed screen-color descriptions; $14/$15 points to the paired color descriptor; $E8 selects normal or lookup-remapped source order
Outputs: writes reconciled packed colors through ($10),Y, ($12),Y, and ($14),Y and merges eight transformed rows through ($0E),Y; palette slots and compositor scratch are updated
Assumptions: all pointers address valid records, the $1200 lookup is resident, and any $14 pointer into $D800 expects I/O-visible color RAM
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, broad compositor scratch including $0A-$41, $BC-$BE, $E3-$E9, and $0112-$011A
Hardware changes: no register writes; writes color RAM when $14/$15 selects the $D800 window, otherwise only RAM

Four selector values 0,1,2,3 used at $1926 after selecting the reconciled palette mapping. Adjacent tables encode the same selector shifted two, four and six bits for constructing one packed bitmap byte.
Four values selector<<2, consumed by the cell compositor while rebuilding a byte from four two-bit palette selectors. Ends at $199A; all entries match the shift formula.
Four values selector<<4, consumed by the cell compositor while rebuilding a byte from four two-bit palette selectors. Ends at $199E; all entries match the shift formula.
Four values selector<<6, consumed by the cell compositor while rebuilding a byte from four two-bit palette selectors. Ends at $19A2; all entries match the shift formula.

Purpose: Count two-bit selector use for an eight-row composite-image record and repeatedly discard the least-used eligible palette sources until enough standard slots are available. Inputs: $0E/$0F points at eight packed selector bytes, $0113-$011A holds their paired selector bytes, $0B-$0D maps three extra selectors, $33-$35 and $E3-$E6 describe candidate availability, $BC-$BE are standard-source eligibility guards, and $41 is the outstanding slot demand. Outputs: $39-$40 contains rebuilt use counts. Zero-use standard sources are marked in $33-$35; least-used eligible standard or extra sources are disabled through $33-$35/$E3-$E6, and $41 is decremented as mappings are released until the available-slot count satisfies it. Assumptions: Each of the eight rows supplies four valid two-bit selectors, selector and mapping indices are in range, and whenever more slots are required at least one eligible nonzero-use candidate exists. Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $22/$23, $33-$35, $39-$41, and $E3-$E6; $0B-$0D and $BC-$BE are read but preserved. Hardware changes: None; the routine only rewrites RAM palette-selection state consumed later by the image renderer.
